title: Imagination: The Workshop of the Mind
coreMove: Ideas are starting capital: use synthetic imagination to combine what exists, invite creative hunches, and keep revising plans until desire has working shape.

exampleSpecs.audience: founders with a product but no demand system
exampleSpecs.stakes: a product remains a curiosity unless the plan multiplies its reach
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a protagonist uses Asa Candler's Coca-Cola case to separate physical material from imagined commercial system

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders who need support before resources exist
exampleSpecs.stakes: supporters need to picture the institution before they can fund it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a protagonist makes a need concrete by following the Gunsaulus sermon pattern

exampleSpecs.stakes: a project fades unless the idea can organize action after the founder leaves
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a protagonist uses Christianity's endurance to test whether an idea can outlive its originator

exampleSpecs.stakes: known resources can remain separate or become a working plan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a protagonist combines existing pieces instead of waiting for pure originality

exampleSpecs.audience: makers who confuse more effort with fresh insight
exampleSpecs.stakes: a failed prototype can become a signal instead of a dead end
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a protagonist treats a hunch as useful only after purpose and contact with the problem have prepared the mind

exampleSpecs.audience: readers defending a first draft too early
exampleSpecs.stakes: the desire can gain shape through revision or stay trapped in a brittle first plan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a protagonist revises a written plan as better combinations appear
